content.text:
I submitted **index 13 (Sb fraction 0.249)** as the best composition. It had the highest EQE I measured, 0.00065%. Every value on this line is extremely low, though, and the top few are close enough that their order may be noise.

**What I measured (all 5 EQE measurements used):**

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.080 | 0.00046 |
| 11 | 0.198 | 0.00062 |
| **13** | **0.249** | **0.00065** |
| 15 | 0.303 | 0.00054 |
| 21 | 0.511 | 0.00023 |

**Why this composition makes sense:**
- EQE was highest around Sb 0.2–0.3 and dropped off on both sides.
- Sb 0.25 is the composition of the compound Bi3SbO7. The band-gap model predicts about 2.27 eV for it, below the 2.7 eV illumination, so it should absorb this light.
- BiSbO4 (Sb 0.5) is predicted at about 3.06 eV, above the illumination energy. That fits the lowest EQE being at index 21.

**What I couldn't confirm:**
- I used 3 of the 5 XRD measurements (indices 9, 13 and 17). None of them clearly matched a single known phase: the best similarity scores were only about 0.5–0.7. So I can't say Bi3SbO7 is actually what formed at index 13. The link rests on composition and the predicted band gap, not on the diffraction data.
- I didn't measure EQE at the Bi-rich end (Sb 0.03–0.06) or at Sb above 0.51. If either region has its own peak, I would have missed it.
